subject: ela
intro: Each item gives you a short informational passage of several paragraphs. The central idea is not stated in one sentence, so you must combine details from across the whole passage to find it. Read carefully, then answer the question. When a question asks for a summary, give an objective summary that states the central idea and key supporting points and leaves out any personal opinion.

items.prompt:
Passage: 'The dollar bills in your wallet do not last forever. A single bill is folded, crushed, and handed from person to person hundreds of times. The oils on people's hands and the constant friction slowly wear away the paper. After about six years, a one dollar bill is usually too worn to use, and larger bills, which change hands less often, can last a few years longer.

Banks collect these tired bills and send them back to the government. There, sorting machines check each bill and pull out the ones that are too damaged. Those bills are shredded into thin strips so they can never be spent again.

The shredded money does not go to waste. Some of it is pressed into building materials such as roofing or insulation. Some is turned into compost for gardens. A few places even mix the strips into souvenir pencils and notepads that people buy as keepsakes. Every year, the government replaces billions of worn bills with crisp new ones, and the old paper begins a second life as something completely different.'

Which statement best expresses the central idea of the passage?
items.answer: Worn out dollar bills are taken out of use and recycled into new products rather than simply thrown away.

steps: No single sentence states the main point, so combine details from across the three paragraphs.

The first paragraph explains that bills wear out, the second explains that worn bills are pulled and shredded, and the third explains that the shredded paper becomes building materials, compost, and pencils.
Put these parts together: the passage is about how old money is removed from use and then recycled into new things.
A statement about bills lasting six years is only one detail from paragraph one, and naming the topic 'money' is too broad, so the full central idea is that worn bills are recycled instead of wasted.

items.prompt:
Passage: 'Octopuses are among the strangest animals in the sea. Start with the basics of the body. An octopus has three hearts and blue blood, and unlike most animals, it has no bones at all. The only hard part of its body is its beak, which means it can squeeze its soft body through any hole larger than that beak, even a gap the size of a coin.

The surprises do not stop there. The octopus's skin is covered with tiny sacs of color that let it change shade in less than a second to match a rock or the sandy floor. Some octopuses go further and copy the shape and movement of other sea animals, such as flatfish or sea snakes, to fool predators into leaving them alone.

These animals are clever as well as strange. Scientists who study octopuses say they can solve puzzles, open jars to reach food, and even remember the faces of the people who feed them. Few creatures combine such an unusual body with such a sharp mind.'

Which statement best expresses the central idea of the passage?
items.answer: The octopus has many unusual body features and abilities that make it one of the most remarkable animals in the sea.

steps: Look at the details across all three paragraphs: three hearts and no bones, a squeezable body, color changing skin, mimicry, and problem solving.
These details all point to the same overall point, that the octopus is unusual and remarkable.
Naming the topic 'octopuses' is too broad because it only names the subject and does not state the author's point.
Choosing only the color changing detail leaves out the others, so the full central idea is that the octopus is remarkable in many ways.

items.prompt:
Passage: 'For most of history, people told time by the sun. A farmer judged the hour by the length of a shadow, and church bells rang when the sun reached its highest point. Because the sun is overhead at slightly different moments in different places, a town might keep its own time, a little different from the next town over. For centuries, this caused no real trouble.

That changed when trains arrived. A train could now cross many towns in a single day, and each town still set its own clock. A train that left one town at noon might reach the next town that still called it eleven forty. Printed schedules became a mess, and serious crashes happened when two trains on the same line thought they were running on different clocks.

In 1883, railroad companies in North America agreed on a solution. They divided the land into time zones, so that all clocks within a zone would read exactly the same. Soon governments made the system official, and the old patchwork of local times faded away for good.'

Which statement best expresses the central idea of the passage?
items.answer: The growth of train travel created the need for standard time zones, which replaced the older system of separate local times.

steps: The passage moves from a problem to a solution across its paragraphs, so the central idea must tie both parts together.
The problem, shown in the first two paragraphs, is that towns kept their own time, which caused confusion and crashes once trains connected them.
The solution, in the last paragraph, is that railroads created time zones so clocks would match.
A statement only about farmers reading shadows covers just the opening, so the central idea must connect the growth of trains to the creation of time zones.

items.prompt:
Passage: 'The desert may look empty, but the kangaroo rat thrives there without ever drinking a drop of water. While most desert animals must search for a water hole, this small rodent never visits one at all. Instead, its entire body is built to hold on to every bit of moisture it has.

The most striking adaptation is inside the animal. The kangaroo rat's kidneys are so powerful that its urine comes out almost as a paste, wasting very little liquid. This lets the rat keep nearly all of the water already inside its body, day after day, even in the driest months.

Its behavior helps too. The kangaroo rat eats mostly dry seeds, which it stuffs into pouches in its cheeks and carries back to its burrow. It sleeps in that cool, deep burrow during the blazing day and comes out only at night, when the air is cooler. Through these adaptations, an animal smaller than your hand survives in one of the harshest places on Earth.'

The central idea is that the kangaroo rat survives in the desert by conserving the water already inside its body. Which detail from the passage best develops this central idea?
items.answer: 'The kangaroo rat's kidneys are so powerful that its urine comes out almost as a paste, wasting very little liquid,' because it gives a specific way the animal's body holds on to the water it already has.

steps: The central idea is about conserving the water already inside the body, so find the detail that shows the body keeping its own water.
The kidney detail directly shows water conservation: the body wastes very little liquid and keeps nearly all of its water.

The detail that the rat eats dry seeds and the detail that it sleeps in a cool burrow describe how it avoids losing extra water or how it behaves, but they do not show the body conserving the water already inside it the way the kidney detail does.
The fact that the rat is smaller than your hand is interesting but says nothing about saving water, so the kidney detail is the single strongest support for this central idea.

items.prompt:
Passage: 'When a volcano erupts, it can change far more than the mountain it sits on. Close to the cone, the danger is plain to see. Hot lava and falling rock destroy forests, bury roads, and flatten homes near the eruption. For the people and animals nearby, the effects are sudden and harsh.

The reach of an eruption, though, can stretch much farther. A large eruption throws ash and gas high into the sky, where winds can carry them for thousands of miles. This ash dims the sun and can cool the whole planet for months. After one huge eruption in 1815, parts of the world had snow in summer and crops failed in places far from the volcano.

Yet the same eruption can give as well as take. Over many years, the ash breaks down into some of the richest farming soil on Earth, and the slopes of old volcanoes often become prized farmland. A volcano can be both a destroyer and, in time, a giver of life.'

Which statement best expresses the central idea of the passage?
items.answer: A volcanic eruption has effects that reach far beyond the mountain, causing both widespread harm and, over time, benefits.

steps: Across the three paragraphs the passage gives details about local destruction, worldwide cooling, and later rich farming soil.
These details show effects both near and far, and both harmful and helpful.
A statement only about lava destroying nearby forests covers just the first paragraph, so it is too narrow.
Combining all the details, the central idea is that an eruption reaches far beyond the mountain and brings both harm and benefit.

items.prompt:
Passage: 'Honeybees do far more than make honey. As a bee moves from flower to flower to gather nectar, yellow dust called pollen sticks to its fuzzy body. The bee then carries this pollen to the next flower it visits. This simple act, called pollination, is how many plants are able to make seeds and fruit.

The scale of this work is huge. Scientists estimate that about one out of every three bites of food people eat depends on bees doing this job. Apples, almonds, blueberries, and melons all need bees to grow. Without pollination, these plants would produce little or no fruit at all.

In recent years, however, bee numbers have dropped sharply in many places. Disease, pesticides, and the loss of wild flowers have all played a part. Farmers worry, because fewer bees means smaller harvests. If bee numbers keep falling, many of the foods now common on our tables could become rare and costly.'

Which statement best expresses the central idea of the passage?
items.answer: Honeybees play a vital role in growing much of the food people eat, so their decline is a serious concern.

steps: Combine the details across the paragraphs: bees spread pollen, that pollen helps plants make fruit, and one in three bites of food depends on it.
The last paragraph adds that bee numbers are dropping and that farmers worry about smaller harvests.
Together these details show that bees matter to our food and that losing them is a problem.
Naming the topic 'honeybees' is too broad, so the central idea is that bees are vital to our food and their decline is concerning.

items.prompt:
Passage: 'Many people picture the Great Wall of China as a single wall built all at once by one powerful emperor. The truth is far more tangled. The wall we know today was built over nearly two thousand years by many different rulers, each adding to the work of those before them.

The earliest walls were simple. Built more than two thousand years ago, they were made of packed earth and were meant only to slow down raiders on horseback. They did not connect to one another and often crumbled within a few generations.

Later rulers thought bigger. They added stone and brick, raised tall towers, and connected separate walls into one long line stretching across the north of the country. Different sections were built in different centuries, using whatever materials were nearby, from earth and wood to heavy stone. What we now call the Great Wall is really many walls, shaped by many hands and joined together over a very long time.'

A student wrote four summaries of the passage. Which is the best objective summary?
items.answer: The Great Wall of China was not built all at once but was constructed over nearly two thousand years by many rulers who added to and joined separate walls using different materials.

steps: An objective summary states the central idea and key supporting points without adding opinion.
The central idea, built across the paragraphs, is that the wall was made over a long time by many rulers, not all at once.
The key points are the long time span, the many builders, the different materials, and the joining of separate walls.

A summary that only mentions the early packed earth walls, or that adds an opinion such as 'it is the greatest wall ever,' would miss the main point or insert judgment, so the complete and objective version is best.

items.prompt:
Passage: 'Light pollution is the glow of artificial light that brightens the night sky. In big cities, the lights of streets, signs, and buildings scatter into the air and wash out the stars. In the most lit places, people may see only a handful of stars where thousands once shone.

This glow does more than spoil the view. It also harms wildlife in surprising ways. Sea turtles that hatch on bright beaches crawl toward the city lights instead of the ocean, and many die before they reach the water. Birds that migrate at night can be drawn off course by lit towers and tall buildings. Even people are affected, sleeping less well when their nights are flooded with light.

The good news is that the problem can be reduced. Many towns are now switching to shielded lamps that point light down at the ground instead of up into the sky. These simple fixes let the stars return, protect migrating animals, and still keep streets safely lit.'

Which statement best expresses the central idea of the passage?
items.answer: Light pollution harms wildlife and people by brightening the night, and using shielded lighting can reduce the problem.

steps: Gather the details across the paragraphs: the glow hides stars, it harms turtles, birds, and people's sleep, and shielded lamps help.
These details show both the harm caused by light pollution and a clear way to reduce it.
A statement only about stars being hidden covers one detail from the first paragraph, not the whole passage.
The full central idea connects the harm to wildlife and people with the solution of shielded lighting.

items.prompt:
Passage: 'The first video games were not sold in any store. In the 1950s and 1960s, they were built by scientists and students on giant computers that filled entire rooms. These machines were research tools, not toys, and only a few people ever saw the games that ran on them.

The early games were simple by today's standards. One famous example let two players bounce a glowing dot back and forth across the screen, a little like tennis. Players had fun, but the computers that ran these games were far too large and far too costly for any ordinary home.

Everything changed in the 1970s. Smaller and cheaper computer chips made it possible to build a game machine that plugged right into a family television. Suddenly, people could play in their own living rooms without a room sized computer or a science degree. A hobby that had lived only in laboratories quickly became something millions of families could enjoy together.'

Which statement best expresses the central idea of the passage?
items.answer: Video games began as experiments on huge laboratory computers and, as technology shrank, became something ordinary families could play at home.

steps: The passage moves from early lab games to home games across its paragraphs, so the central idea covers that change.
Key details are that the first games ran on room sized research computers and that smaller chips later made home games possible.
A statement only about the tennis like dot game covers just one example, so it is too narrow.
Combining the details, the central idea is the shift from laboratory machines to games families could play at home.

items.prompt:
Passage: 'Coral reefs are sometimes called the rainforests of the sea, and the nickname fits. Though they cover less than one percent of the ocean floor, about one quarter of all ocean species depend on them at some point in their lives. Fish hide from predators and breed among the branching coral.

Reefs matter to people as well as to fish. Coastal communities around the world rely on reefs for food and for the income that comes from fishing and tourism. Millions of people earn a living from the waters around healthy reefs. Reefs even guard the coastline itself, breaking the force of large waves before they crash onto the shore.

Because so much depends on them, the loss of the world's reefs would not be a small or local problem. Warming oceans and pollution are already damaging reefs in many places. If they disappeared, the effects would ripple through the ocean and through the lives of millions of people who depend on them.'

A student wrote this draft summary: 'Coral reefs are home to many ocean species and help people through food, money, and protection from waves. We absolutely must save them before it is too late.' Which sentence or phrase in the summary should be removed to make it objective?
items.answer: 'We absolutely must save them before it is too late,' because it is a personal opinion or call to action, not an objective statement of what the passage says.

steps: An objective summary reports what the text says and leaves out the writer's opinions or commands.
The first sentence of the draft fairly states the central idea and key points from the passage.
The second sentence, 'We absolutely must save them before it is too late,' urges action and shows the writer's feelings.
Because that line is an opinion the passage never states, it should be removed to keep the summary objective.

items.prompt:
Passage: 'For years, drivers complained that one stretch of city highway flooded every spring. As soon as the snow melted, water pooled across the lanes, slowing traffic and forcing crews to close the road. The flooding returned in the same spot, spring after spring.

At first, the city tried the obvious fix. Workers tore up the pavement and put in bigger storm drains, hoping to carry the water away faster. The cost was high, but the next spring the water still pooled just as before. The drains were not solving the real problem.

Finally, engineers studied the land itself and found the true cause. The road had been built straight across an old streambed. When the snow melted each year, the water simply returned to its natural path, right where the highway now sat. Instead of fighting the stream, the city built a wide channel beside the road to guide the water away. The next spring, for the first time in years, the highway stayed completely dry.'

Which statement best expresses the central idea of the passage?
items.answer: The city solved the highway flooding only after engineers found the real cause, an old streambed under the road, and worked with the water instead of against it.

steps: The passage moves from a failed fix to a successful one across its paragraphs, so the central idea covers the whole story.
Bigger drains failed because they did not address the cause, which was the old streambed under the road.
The real solution was to build a channel that guided the water along its natural path.
A statement only about bigger drains being added covers one failed attempt, so the central idea must include finding the cause and the working solution.

items.prompt:
Passage: 'A small country called Bhutan, tucked in the mountains of Asia, measures its success in an unusual way. Most nations judge how well they are doing by tracking how much money they make each year. Bhutan tracks something different, a goal it calls Gross National Happiness.

In practice, this changes how the country makes decisions. Before approving new roads or factories, officials ask whether the project will protect the land, keep families close, and preserve old traditions, not just whether it will add money. A plan that would bring wealth but harm the country's way of life can be turned down.

Bhutan has acted on this idea more than once. The country has refused some businesses and projects that would have earned a great deal of money but damaged its forests or rivers. To its leaders, a healthy environment and a contented people are worth more than a larger pile of cash. Money matters, they say, but it is not the only measure of a good life.'

Which statement best expresses the central idea of the passage?
items.answer: Bhutan measures its success by the happiness and well being of its people and land rather than only by money.

steps: Combine the details across the paragraphs: Bhutan tracks Gross National Happiness, weighs land and tradition over money, and refuses harmful business.
These details all show that Bhutan values happiness and a healthy environment above wealth.
Naming the topic 'Bhutan' is too broad and does not state the author's point about how the country measures success.
The central idea is that Bhutan measures success by well being rather than only by money.

items.prompt:
Passage: 'The cane toad was supposed to be a helper. In 1935, farmers in Australia brought the large toad in from another country to eat the beetles that were destroying their sugar cane crops. On paper, the plan looked clever and cheap.

In the field, it failed almost at once. The beetles lived high on the cane stalks, far above the ground, and the heavy toads simply could not reach them. The pests kept eating the crops while the toads sat below, useless against the very problem they were meant to fix.

Worse was still to come. The toads bred quickly and spread across the country in huge numbers. Their skin holds a strong poison, so native animals that try to eat them often sicken and die. With no natural enemies in Australia to keep them in check, the toads kept multiplying and moving into new regions. A creature brought in to solve one problem ended up creating a much larger one that the country still struggles with today.'

Which statement best expresses the central idea of the passage?
items.answer: A plan to use cane toads to protect crops backfired, and the toads became a far bigger problem than the one they were meant to solve.

steps: The passage tells how a plan failed and then made things worse, so the central idea covers both the plan and its result.
Across the paragraphs, the toads could not reach the beetles, then they bred fast, poisoned other animals, and spread with no enemies.
A statement only about why farmers brought the toads covers the beginning, not the harmful outcome.
The full central idea is that the toad plan backfired and created a larger problem.

items.prompt:
Passage: 'Public libraries are changing, and the change goes far beyond the books on the shelves. For a long time, a library was mainly a quiet place to borrow novels and look things up. Today, many libraries lend far more than books.

Walk into a modern branch and you may be surprised by what you can check out. Some libraries let people borrow tools, telescopes, or musical instruments. Others have turned spare rooms into spaces where visitors can record music or print three dimensional models. The shelves now hold objects that no library would have offered a generation ago.

Libraries are offering new services as well. Many run free classes in skills like coding or job hunting, and anyone with a library card can join at no cost. Yet librarians say the basic goal has not changed at all. As one put it, the aim is the same as it always was, to give everyone equal access to knowledge and useful tools, even if the things on the shelves are different now.'

A student wrote four summaries. Which is the best objective summary of the passage?
items.answer: Modern public libraries now lend many items beyond books and offer free classes and equipment, continuing their goal of giving everyone equal access to knowledge.

steps: A good objective summary states the central idea and the key supporting points without opinion.
The central idea, built across the paragraphs, is that libraries have expanded beyond books while keeping their goal of equal access.
Key points are lending tools and instruments, offering classes and recording or printing equipment, and the unchanged goal of access to knowledge.
A summary that lists only one service, or that adds a judgment like 'this is the best change ever,' would be incomplete or biased, so the complete, opinion free version is best.

items.prompt:
Passage: 'Most plants make their food from sunlight alone, but the Venus flytrap does something stranger. This unusual plant also eats insects. It grows in bogs where the soil is poor and lacks the nitrogen and other nutrients that plants usually pull from the ground. To survive in this thin, hungry soil, the flytrap has found another way to get what it needs.

Its trap is famous. Each leaf forms a pair of pink pads lined with tiny trigger hairs. When an insect touches two hairs in a row, the trap snaps shut in less than a second, locking the bug inside. The plant then slowly digests its catch over about a week before reopening to wait for its next meal.

This strange diet is what lets the flytrap live where other plants cannot. By catching insects, it makes up for the nutrients the bog soil cannot give it. In this way, a plant that would starve in ordinary conditions thrives in one of the poorest soils on Earth.'

The central idea is that the Venus flytrap eats insects to make up for the nutrients it cannot get from the poor soil where it grows. Which detail from the passage best develops this central idea?
items.answer: 'It grows in bogs where the soil is poor and lacks the nitrogen and other nutrients that plants usually pull from the ground,' because it explains why the plant must catch insects in the first place.

steps: The central idea explains why the flytrap eats insects: the soil is too poor to give it the nutrients it needs, so look for the detail that gives that reason.
The line about the bog soil being poor and lacking nutrients states exactly why the plant needs another food source, which is the heart of the central idea.

The detail that the trap snaps shut in less than a second and the detail that the plant digests its catch over about a week describe how the plant catches and breaks down its food, but they do not explain why the plant must eat insects at all.
Because the central idea is about replacing the nutrients the soil cannot provide, the detail about the poor bog soil best develops it.
